summary: Compare finite supplied signal plans on an open movement network with explicit arrivals, routes, storage and saturation-service inputs, without reusing closed-lane car-following physics.
objective: Compare finite supplied signal plans on an open movement network with explicit arrivals, routes, storage and saturation-service inputs, without reusing closed-lane car-following physics.
example_prompts: Build open-boundary signal queue playback with explicit stable IDs, units, time, boundary inputs and stale/unavailable states.
not_for: Safety certification, regulatory compliance, or operational control without qualified local review.

entities.name: Movement queues
entities.guidance: Define stable incoming-to-outgoing movement IDs, integer external arrivals per step, finite storage and a fixed downstream route.

entities.name: Signal plans
entities.guidance: Store cycle epoch, phase intervals and permitted movements; reject conflicting simultaneously green movements using a supplied conflict matrix.

entities.name: Service ledger
entities.guidance: Accumulate green service credit from supplied saturation flow and discharge whole vehicles only when queue and downstream storage permit.

state_contract.model: Accept a finite directed movement graph, step dt>0 seconds, horizon H, nonnegative integer external arrivals a[m,k], finite integer storage, fixed routes, supplied saturation rate s[m] vehicles/hour and periodic phase plan with explicit epoch. Each step snapshots all queues/storage, admits boundary arrivals into a next buffer, and computes all movement departures from the snapshot. Only a green movement accrues fractional credit c:=frac(c+s*dt/3600); its whole service opportunities are min(queue,floor(previous_fraction+s*dt/3600),downstream free reservations). Unused whole opportunities are discarded, red resets credit to zero, and retained credit is always in [0,1). For movements competing for the same downstream storage, allocate the snapshot-derived demands in a supplied stable reservation priority, record denied reservations, complete all reservations, then commit every departure/arrival once so no vehicle traverses multiple movements in one step. Mark rejected arrivals/spillback separately. Compare plans only with byte-identical arrivals, routes, storage, rates, reservation priority, horizon and initial queues.
state_contract.authority: Boundary arrivals, routing, storage, conflict matrix, stable reservation priority and plan epoch own traffic state. Blender/glTF supplies named roads, stop lines and signal heads; Three.js owns snapshot demand, deterministic reservations, queue/service arithmetic, phase state, rejected arrivals and exact reset.
actions: Choose one of two supplied plans.
Reset common demand, initial queues, service credits, reservation priority and plan epoch.

invariants: Vehicle conservation includes external arrivals, queues, in-network transfers, exits and explicitly rejected arrivals.
Red movements discharge zero and reset service credit; retained green fractional credit always lies in [0,1), with unused whole opportunities discarded.
All movement discharges use one queue snapshot and simultaneous downstream reservations; a vehicle moves at most one movement per step.
No movement exceeds supplied saturation service credit.
Plan comparison changes only phase schedule.
motion_guidance: Playback restores stored model/event steps; animation between steps is explanatory and never changes authoritative counts, timestamps or completion state.
creative_affordances: Use cutaways, small multiples, queues and non-color status glyphs while keeping assumptions and unavailable states visible.
known_limits: A coarse deterministic queue model: no car following, lane changing, startup stochasticity, pedestrians, calibration, prediction or signal approval.

claims.statement: The FHWA Traffic Signal Timing Manual describes red-time queue formation, green-time discharge approaching saturation flow, oversaturation when arrivals exceed service, and movement capacity as saturation flow multiplied by effective-green ratio.
claims.scope: FHWA-HOP-08-024 Chapter 3 operational principles; this recipe’s discrete credits, storage and routing are authored simplifications.

object_craft.structure: Blender authors named approach lanes, stop lines, signal heads and reusable vehicle glyphs at neutral transforms; glTF carries stable movement IDs only.
object_craft.material: Phase, queue and spillback use shape/pattern plus hue; glow never means measured flow.
object_craft.articulation: Three.js binds external arrivals/routes, updates service credits and queues, places representative vehicles from counts and resets common inputs.

physical_contract.scope: Open-boundary aggregate movement queues; no microscopic vehicle dynamics.
physical_contract.timestep: Fixed dt seconds with snapshot, boundary-admission, simultaneous service/reservation, then one commit.
checks: Continuous green opportunities match s*duration/3600 up to discarded idle/block capacity and retained fractional credit <1; red resets credit.
Two plans share identical non-plan hashes.
